item.title: California gunman repeatedly released before deadly rampage, fiery shootout with deputies
item.description: Derek Spencer was arrested three times and released in Sacramento County in the weeks before he allegedly gunned down Cheryl Macy in Placer County.
item.content:encoded:
A California murder suspect was arrested three times in less than two weeks and walked out of jail after each bust before authorities said his crime spree ended with an innocent woman dead and a fiery shootout with deputies.

Prosecutors said they tried to keep Derek Spencer, 44, behind bars after he allegedly assaulted a Sacramento County sheriff’s deputy. Instead, he posted bail, was arrested twice more and was released both times before allegedly killing 76-year-old Cheryl Macy, a beloved former Placer County District Attorney’s Office employee.

"Sadly, this should never have occurred but bail reform in California has prioritized criminal offenders over victims," the Sacramento County District Attorney’s Office said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

Spencer was ultimately killed early Monday after allegedly opening fire on Placer County sheriff’s deputies during a tense standoff in the rugged forest near Iowa Hill.

MANHUNT UNDERWAY IN CALIFORNIA AFTER ARMED SUSPECT ALLEGEDLY POINTS GUN AT PEOPLE, SHOOTS AT OFFICERS

Authorities said he also set two fires as tactical teams closed in, forcing an overnight helicopter rescue of three SWAT operators threatened by the flames.

VIDEO SHOWS POLICE TAKE DOWN COP KILLER WITH ARMORED VEHICLE AFTER GUNMAN TURNED NEIGHBORHOOD INTO WAR ZONE

The deadly chain of events followed a string of arrests and releases that prosecutors said exposed dangerous gaps in California’s bail system.

The first arrest came Sept. 3, when Sacramento County deputies accused Spencer of felony vandalism, resisting arrest and assaulting a deputy with a deadly weapon.

CHARLOTTE REPEAT OFFENDER CHARGED WITH KILLING MAN HOURS AFTER RELEASE ON BOND

The Sacramento County DA’s office filed charges Sept. 8, including felony assault with a deadly weapon likely to cause great bodily injury and attempting, through threats and violence, to prevent the deputy from carrying out official duties.

Prosecutors asked that Spencer remain in custody, but a judge set bail as required by law, the DA’s office said. Spencer posted it and was released Sept. 11.

REPEAT OFFENDER BUSTED AGAIN LESS THAN 24 HOURS AFTER RELEASE IN BRAZEN JEWELRY STORE THEFT CASE: POLICE

Then the arrests kept coming.

At about 11 p.m. Sept. 13, Folsom police responded to an alarm at a model home in the 4600 block of Dehone Circle. Officers encountered Spencer walking out of the property and arrested him on suspicion of burglary, the department told Fox News Digital.

ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED WITH BRUTAL SLAYING ONE DAY AFTER CALIFORNIA JUDGE RELEASED HIM: DHS

He was booked into the Sacramento County Main Jail and released on his own recognizance the following day, prosecutors said.

Two days later, Sacramento County deputies arrested Spencer again, this time on suspicion of stealing a vehicle. He posted bail and was back out of custody Sept. 17.

HOW A NONCITIZEN SUSPECTED KILLER GOT CAUGHT AND RELEASED BY NEWSOM-APPOINTED JUDGE: TIMELINE

By then, Spencer was also due in court for a preliminary hearing in the deputy-assault case. He failed to appear Sept. 18, prompting a judge to issue a warrant, according to the DA’s office.

Prosecutors were still reviewing the burglary and vehicle-theft reports for possible charges when Spencer’s alleged rampage moved into neighboring counties.

Authorities said Spencer stole another vehicle and guns and fired at a moving vehicle in El Dorado County on Sept. 19. The next day, Placer County deputies began hunting for him after he allegedly pointed a gun at victims.

Deputies spotted Spencer in the Iowa Hill area, but he allegedly rammed a sheriff’s patrol vehicle and escaped. Authorities said he later fired at deputies and law enforcement helicopters, triggering an intensive manhunt and warnings for residents to lock their doors and stay inside.

As tactical teams cleared a home where Spencer had been seen, they found Macy shot to death inside. Investigators believe Spencer killed her before fleeing into the surrounding forest. Authorities have not publicly identified any prior connection between the two.

REMAINING SUSPECT IN TUCSON POLICE CADET KILLING CAPTURED AFTER FIVE-DAY MANHUNT

A California Highway Patrol aircraft using infrared technology located Spencer shortly before 2:30 a.m. Monday, according to the Placer County Sheriff’s Office. Several tactical teams spent hours moving through the steep, heavily wooded terrain in darkness to reach him.

When deputies approached, Spencer opened fire, authorities said. A standoff followed, and drone video allegedly captured him starting two separate fires.

At about 4 a.m., Spencer fired again from behind a berm, prompting deputies to return fire and fatally strike him, the sheriff’s office said.

The flames soon threatened SWAT operators in the forest. A tactical flight crew from the Washoe County Sheriff’s Office RAVEN aviation unit flew through darkness and low-visibility conditions to hoist three operators out of the area.

The unit said the mission relied on a specialized night-hoist capability available to only a limited number of law enforcement aviation teams in the region.

The Placer County Sheriff’s Office called the case a "dangerous crime spree that took a tragic turn, resulting in the loss of an innocent life."

The Sacramento County DA’s office pointed to the California Supreme Court’s recent Kowalczyk decision, arguing that it has limited judges’ ability to detain repeat offenders before trial, even when they may pose a danger.

"While the District Attorney’s Office has and will continue to argue that dangerous and repeat offenders like Derek Spencer remain in custody, California must repeal the Kowalczyk decision and change the law to prioritize victims when addressing bail," the office said.

The Placer County DA’s office separately said Spencer’s repeated releases raised "serious questions" about whether state law and recent court decisions give judges enough power to prevent similar tragedies.

"As prosecutors, our responsibility is not only to seek justice after someone is harmed, but to speak plainly when the system presents warning signs that cannot be ignored," the office said.

Macy served the Placer County DA’s office from 2006 to 2020 and remained a cherished part of its extended family. She was also a mother, grandmother and great-grandmother.

Placer County District Attorney Morgan Gire honored Macy at a county Board of Supervisors meeting Wednesday, telling community leaders that her death had left his office and the wider community heartbroken.

BAKERSFIELD, CALIFORNIA HOSTAGE STANDOFF ENDS AFTER FBI KILLS ARMED SEX OFFENDER

Gire called for answers, transparency and accountability while urging the community to remember how Macy lived rather than how she died. His office said former colleagues remembered the energy she brought to her work, the warmth she showed others and the lasting impact she made across Placer County.

"The loss of Cheryl is devastating to our office and to the entire community," the office said. "Our hearts are with her family, her friends, and everyone who knew and loved her."

Her granddaughter, Addison, told KCRA that Macy had a special way of hugging her loved ones: three squeezes to say, "I love you."

"She was the only person who’s ever done that and told me that," Addison said, calling it a memory she will always carry.

The fatal deputy-involved shooting and Macy’s death remain under investigation.

item.title: New York Islanders set to unleash culinary 'disasterpiece' on unsuspecting fans this season
item.description: The New York Islanders unveiled a Nerds Gummy Clusters grilled cheese sandwich, and the bizarre arena concession item is turning heads and stomachs.
item.content:encoded:
Most of us are taught at a pretty young age that just because you like two separate things doesn't mean combining them makes an awesome new entity.

For example, you may love your wife while also being a big fan of grabbing some drinks with your college boys, but combining the two is probably not the best idea in the world.

This applies to food too, as you wouldn't catch me combining pickles with a chocolate milkshake, despite my love for both.

VEGAS GOLDEN KNIGHTS BUST OUT THE CONCESSION STAND BIG GUNS FOR STANLEY CUP FINAL

Why, then, on God's green earth, did the New York Islanders think it would be a swell idea to put Nerds Gummy Clusters in grilled cheese and call it an edible concession item?

Someone get me a bucket!

I like grilled cheese.

I'm also a big fan of Nerds Gummy Clusters.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

But maybe we should keep these two things on separate ends of the meal spectrum, where they belong.

What is it with sports arenas and combining the most bizarrely incompatible food items they can think of?

It's almost as if we are in some sort of culinary arms race, and all these teams are trying to outdo one another to try and drum up some press clippings (which I'm clearly contributing to).

My mom always told me not to knock something until I try it, but I think I'll skip the Nerds grilled cheese abomination and just assume I'm not a fan.

The sad thing is that there has to be a market for these Frankenstein-esque creations, otherwise these arenas would stop making them altogether.

If you're reading this and you happen to be one of the sickos that would willingly try something like a Nerds grilled cheese sandwich, do me a favor: don't.

I'd like to be able to go more than a month or two without seeing the worst menu item on the face of the planet and then getting worked up into a frenzy having to write about it.

The beautiful thing about capitalism is we can make this stuff go away by just not buying it.

So the next time you're at an Islanders game, maybe opt for the plastic hockey stick filled with beer or some nachos out of a goalie mask.

And let me keep a sliver of my sanity this hockey season.
